resources.string: Ringomote acts as a Bluetooth remote for your Apple TV. To do that, it needs permission to connect to and be found by nearby devices. Nothing leaves your phone except the button presses sent to your Apple TV.
Permission was not granted. If the system no longer asks, allow “Nearby devices” in the app settings.
This phone cannot act as a Bluetooth Low Energy input device, so it cannot control an Apple TV.
Ringomote could not start advertising as a Bluetooth remote. Another app may be using all of the phone’s Bluetooth advertising. Close that app and try again.
Not connected. A paired Apple TV reconnects by itself once it is awake; to pair a new one, pick this phone in its Bluetooth settings.
Connected to %1$s. To disconnect, remove this phone in the Apple TV’s Bluetooth settings; the phone cannot end the link itself.

On the Apple TV, open Settings > Remotes and Devices > Bluetooth and choose this phone. Accept the pairing request on the phone, then open the notification shade, tap the Bluetooth pairing notification and confirm the 6-digit code.
This phone has no screen for that Bluetooth setting.
Take the colours from your wallpaper. When off, Ringomote uses its own coral palette.
How the remote fills the screen.
Pairing with an Apple TV happens on the TV. To remove a paired Apple TV from this phone, open the phone’s Bluetooth settings and forget it there.
Use your phone as a remote for Apple TV, compatible with the Siri Remote (1st generation).

Ringomote has no internet permission and collects no data. Button presses go only to your Apple TV, directly over Bluetooth. The app stores only your appearance settings and whether it has connected before.
